messages:
maya: heads-up — dedicated-west1 pool is at sustained 100% GPU util and we're seeing spot preemptions. k8s is starting preemptive drains on older nodes, low-priority org queues are growing. can ops run a controlled shift to hosted?

julian: ack. i've seen OOMs + node reboots in the past 10m. what's the cadence you want for the shift? slow increments or full cutover?

maya: slow. prefer quiet drain -> move non-critical traffic first. plan: mark nodes unschedulable, then increment hosted routing weight in 10% steps every 30s while watching error/latency. if errors spike, rollback to previous weight.

sam: i'll do the weight shifts. doing increments 0.1 -> 0.2 -> 0.3 etc. command I'll run: `rbctl routes set-weight --region west1 --to-hosted 0.1` then repeat. will post statuses.

lee: note that the dedicated auto-scaler for west1 is disabled for planned maintenance — re-enable takes ~12-15m. so we can't rely on auto-scale to absorb this.

manually-reproduced log from node-abc123:
```
[2026-08-21T14:02:11Z] grpc: stream reset: rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = GPU memory OOM
[2026-08-21T14:02:12Z] kubelet: eviction signal: memory.available < threshold
[2026-08-21T14:02:13Z] scheduler: pod evicted, preemptive-drain initiated on node-abc123
```

julian: thanks — that matches what I'm seeing. agree with gradual. also we should prefer routing filter by org priority so critical customers aren't touched.

anita: approve emergency shift. cost FYI: hosted burst will increase bill; estimate +18% for the hour depending on token volume. OK to proceed?

maya: approved for up to 2 hours. prioritize orgs tagged `non-critical` and `test` first. ops, can you filter by priority <=2?

sam: yes. using the priority filter: `rbctl routes promote --region west1 --to-hosted --filter "priority<=2" --step 0.1 --wait 30s`

ops-bot: deploy-bot: route-change queued: add hosted weight +0.1 for west1 (filter: priority<=2).

sam: step1 applied -> hosted weight +0.1 (hosted:10% / dedicated:90%). monitoring now.

julian: seeing RTT bump ~20ms for some endpoints, but no 5xxs yet. caches warming slightly slower.

maya: copy. after step2 we'll check token rate and cache misses. if token cost climbs >25% from baseline, pause.

sam: step2 applied -> hosted weight 0.2. metrics: error rate stable, token/sec +6%, cost projection +9% for 30m.

julian: small thing — KV cache miss rate for low-priority orgs up ~12%, causing more prefix recompute. tracking on dashboard `infra/cache/west1`.

maya: enabling prefix caching for non-critical orgs now: `cachectl enable --org-tag non-critical --prefix true`. should reduce repeated token churn.

lee: can we request a short-lived dedicated burst while this stabilizes? policy allows emergency burst of up to 4x small-GPU nodes for 30-120m with infra approval. cost vs hosted tradeoff?

anita: approved a 2-hour burst if it materially reduces hosted egress spend. maya, julian — are the 4 nodes worth it?

julian: might help with hot shards, but given node churn and preemptions, host pool may be less stable. I'd prefer the weight-shift + caching first and reassess in 10m.

sam: step3 applied -> hosted weight 0.3. latency stable, no 5xxs. continuing.

maya: quick ops playbook reminder: to unschedule gracefully we use `kubectl cordon node-xyz` then `kubectl drain node-xyz --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` (do not use `--force` unless we must). also set taint: `kubectl taint nodes node-xyz dedicated-drain=planned:NoSchedule` so we avoid immediate reschedules.

sam: noted. running final step to 0.4 now.

sam: step4 complete -> hosted weight 0.4. the backlog for priority<=2 orgs dropped 82% in queue length. nice.

julian: observing cache warm-up, prefix cache reduced misses by ~9% after `cachectl` toggle. token cost delta now +11% (within maya's limit).

anita: sounds good. keep an eye on billing dashboard, tag any unexpected spikes.

maya: i've filed SR# 34892 with infra-ops for emergency capacity request (4x gpus) — ETA 18m. if they come up we can start draining fewer nodes and shift traffic back incrementally.

sam: will hold additional rollback commands ready: `rbctl routes set-weight --region west1 --to-hosted 0.0` to fully revert, and `rbctl routes set-weight --region west1 --to-hosted 0.5` if we need to scale further.

ops-bot: alert suppressed: dedicated/west1/high-gpu-util -> routing mitigation in progress.

maya: summary: 1) grad shift non-critical -> hosted 40% done, 2) prefix caching enabled for non-critical orgs, 3) burst request filed, 4) k8s drains are running with taints. leaving thread open until nodes stable or burst completes.

sam: standing by watching metrics. i'll post again on any anomalies. :thumbsup:

julian: +1. we'll follow up with a short postmortem if this becomes recurring.

ops-bot: automated note: incident window opened (2076543210 -> ongoing).
